items.title: Slipway 0.0.52: Making Production Boring Again
items.summary: Slipway 0.0.52 is a production-hardening release spanning more than 50 pull requests: safer deployments, a Sails-native application backend, a serious production workspace, release controls, and much clearer failure boundaries.

items.title: Waterline Transactions in Sails.js: History, API, and Real-World Usage
items.summary: Learn Waterline transactions in Sails.js: history, database transaction basics, .transaction(), .usingConnection(), adapter support, and real-world examples.

items.title: The Boring Stack 1.5.0
items.summary: The Boring JavaScript Stack 1.5.0 brings stable Inertia v3 support, rsbuild-plugin-inertia, selective SSR, Precognition, richer deferred props, preserved fragments, Youch-powered development errors, and production Inertia error pages.

items.title: Migrating a Boring Stack Test to Sounding: From Split Tools to One Calm Trial
items.summary: I migrated African Engineer from a split testing story built around Playwright, custom Sails bootstrapping, and ad hoc helpers to one Sounding-powered test() API. Here is what changed, and why it reads better.

items.title: Introducing Sounding: A Sails-Native Testing Framework for The Boring JavaScript Stack
items.summary: Sounding gives Sails applications one calm testing story: one test() API, one Sails-centered trial context, first-class Inertia and mail testing, and browser flows only when the browser actually matters.

items.title: Real-Time with SSE the Sails Way
items.summary: When you hear real-time in Sails, you think WebSockets. But there's another way — Server-Sent Events. Here's how I went from polling to SSE to a custom Sails hook in Slipway, and when you should use each.

items.title: Durable UI Patterns
items.summary: Durable UI is a set of patterns for building interfaces that survive refreshes, navigation, and real users. A practical guide to state placement, cleanup contracts, and UI that doesn't break.

items.title: Introducing Durable UI: The 30% That Vibe Coding Can't Teach You
items.summary: Your AI writes the component. But does it survive a refresh? Durable UI is a new Sailscasts course that teaches the state placement decisions no LLM can make for you.

items.title: Introducing Slipway - The Complete Deployment Platform for Sails.js & The Boring JavaScript Stack
items.summary: Slipway is an open-source, self-hosted platform purpose-built for Sails.js and The Boring JavaScript Stack. Deploy, manage, monitor, and debug your apps on your own infrastructure with one command.

items.title: The Boring Stack 1.0.0
items.summary: The Boring JavaScript Stack 1.0 is here with a complete architectural overhaul: AsyncLocalStorage for request isolation, once() props for intelligent caching, and a suite of new APIs that make building full-stack JavaScript apps even more boring (in the best way).

items.title: Introducing Shipwright - The Modern Asset Pipeline for Sails.js
items.summary: Say goodbye to Grunt. Shipwright brings Rsbuild-powered bundling to Sails with 10x faster builds, TypeScript support, and Hot Module Replacement out of the box.

items.title: Wish 1.0.0
items.summary: Wish 1.0.0 is here with a simplified configuration, automatic environment variable detection, and support for multiple instances of the same provider.

items.title: Understanding Parley: The Deferred Pattern Powering Sails
items.summary: Parley is a lightweight flow control library that powers async operations across the Sails ecosystem. Learn how this pre-Promise Deferred pattern enables timeout and error negotiation in Waterline models and Sails helpers.

items.title: Implementing Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) in The Boring JavaScript Stack
items.summary: Learn how to implement fair, region-based pricing in your Sails.js application using Purchasing Power Parity. A step-by-step guide to making your products accessible globally while maintaining sustainable revenue.

items.title: Introducing Quest - Elegant Job Scheduling for Sails.js
items.summary: Meet Quest, the job scheduler that brings elegant, human-readable scheduling to your Sails.js applications with full access to models, helpers, and configuration.

items.title: Session Management Over WebSockets in Sails
items.summary: Explore how Sails.js manages user sessions over persistent WebSocket connections, ensuring secure and consistent authentication for both browser and native clients.

items.title: The Virtual Request Pattern in Sails.js
items.summary: A technical examination of how Sails.js uses virtual requests to handle HTTP and WebSocket protocols with a single codebase, eliminating duplication.

items.title: Understanding Sails WebSockets: A Modern, Unified Approach to Real-Time in Node.js
items.summary: A practical introduction to how Sails.js handles WebSockets: from the virtual request pattern to JWR responses, and why the sails-hook-sockets approach is a game-changer for real-time Node.js apps.

items.title: Waterline Query Stages
items.summary: Discover how Waterline processes your queries through a multi-stage pipeline—validating, normalizing, and transforming them for reliable, database-agnostic execution.

items.title: Waterline Features
items.summary: Learn about Waterline Features — optional, database-specific capabilities like unique constraints, auto-increment, spatial data, and cross-adapter operations that extend core ORM functionality.

items.title: Connections and Datastores in Waterline
items.summary: Learn the difference between connections and datastores in Sails.js. See how Waterline uses them to manage database configuration and scale apps across multiple databases.

items.title: Waterline Interfaces
items.summary: Learn how Waterline interfaces define the contract between models and adapters. Discover why interfaces matter and how they keep your Sails.js app database-agnostic.

items.title: How I Implemented Transactions in sails-disk (Without Native DB Support)
items.summary: sails-disk doesn’t support native transactions, so I built a snapshot-based system that adds commit/rollback capabilities. Here’s how I designed, implemented, and tested transaction support in a file-based adapter for Sails.js.

items.title: Waterline Adapters
items.summary: Discover how Waterline adapters let your models connect to MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, SQLite, and more. Learn why adapters matter and how they power Waterline’s database-agnostic design.

items.title: What is Waterline?
items.summary: Waterline is a database-agnostic ORM for Node.js that lets you define models once and use them across MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, and more with a single API.

items.title: Controlling What Your Models Send Back with customToJSON()
items.summary: Learn how to use customToJSON in Sails.js models to control what data gets sent back in yor Sails responses. We’ll cover why it’s useful, how to hide sensitive fields like passwords or tokens, and show practical examples you can drop into your project.

items.title: Powering toast notifications in The Boring JavaScript Stack with Flash messages
items.summary: Learn how to streamline notifications in your The Boring JavaScript Stack apps by unifying flash messages and toast notifications. Discover a practical approach to reduce duplication, ensure consistency, and simplify your codebase for a smoother developer experience.

items.title: Sails.js Launches Official Community Space on Discord
items.summary: Sails.js announces the official Sails.js Discord community! Join now to connect with developers, get the latest release updates, and help revitalize the Sails ecosystem.

items.summary: After working with Express for a while, I was introduced to Sails after joining the Sailscasts community. I have come to like Sails and I want to say why in this article.

items.title: Rate limiting in Sails
items.summary: Rate limiting helps you control the rate of incoming requests to an API. In this article we go over how to set up rate limiting in Sails

items.title: Sails for Express developers - Routing
items.summary: Part 1 of the Sails for Express developers series of article aimed at showing how Express developers can use Sails today.

items.title: Setting up API monitoring with Treblle in Sails
items.summary: I recently discovered Treblle - an API monitoring service that let's you monitor your APIs in production. Here is how to set it up in a Sails project.

items.summary: I have been researching Playwright for a while now and finally decided to take the plunge and set up end-to-end testing in the sailscasts.com codebase with it. Let me show you how I did it.

items.summary: The vision of Sailscasts is to empower anyone with a basic idea of JavaScript to build fullstack Node.js applications. With the new docs we hope to provide great documentation for the technologies we build to foster this vision

items.summary: The second Sailsconf - a global conference for the Sails community goes live in a couple of days

items.title: Using the paginate query modifier method for pagination
items.summary: Sails provides a super useful syntactic sugar for paginating Waterline queries. In this article we will see how to get started using it in your applications.

items.title: Testing your Sails apps with Japa
items.summary: Japa is an API-first testing framework. It focuses only on testing Node.js (backend) applications, thus resulting in a fast, small, and simple tests runner.
